text: Describe a time when you solved a problem creatively.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Problem Solving & Data-Driven Decisions): Describe a time when you solved a problem creatively.

[PRIMARY] EX-09 | Conversational Search — Proxy Item Breakthrough
  situation: In our LLM-powered conversational search project, query rewrites generated by the LLM consistently failed to find relevant results because the LLM's "world knowledge" didn't match our search engine's tokenizer and parser behavior -- plausible-sounding queries returned irrelevant or empty results.
  task: I needed to find a way to bridge the gap between LLM-generated intent and the existing search infrastructure, unblocking the project quickly.
  action: - Diagnosed the root cause: the LLM generated semantically correct queries, but the search engine's word segmentation and keyword interpretation mangled them into irrelevant results - Instead of fixing LLM query generation or retraining the search engine (both expensive, slow), discovered the proxy item approach: have the LLM generate descriptions of ideal items for each sub-intent, then use these as proxy items for ANN-based retrieval - This maximally leveraged existing infrastructure (embedding search, retrieval pipelines) with zero changes to the search engine - Each sub-intent got its own 
  result: The proxy item approach delivered strong results and was the **fastest path to unblocking experimentation**. It demonstrated maximum reuse of existing infrastructure while elegantly solving the LLM-search adaptation gap -- a solution that would have taken months via the alternatives.
  evidence_quotes: ["User: LLM的所谓world knowledge没有办法很好的adapt to我们的search", "User: 简单的传递keyword可能被我们的search engine误解并且断句断词得到不相关的结果", "User: 发现了proxy item得到了很好的结果，实现了对于已有infra和技术的最大程度利用和最快的test unblock"]
  cn_elevator_pitch: LLM query rewrite 因 tokenizer 不匹配持续返回无关结果；提出 proxy item 方案——让 LLM 生成理想商品描述再用向量匹配，最大化复用现有 infra 快速 unblock 实验 | KEY FACTS: LLM-search 适配鸿沟 | proxy item 方案 | 最大化现有 infra 复用 | 最快 unblock 路径

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- EX-01 | Search Diversity --- Intent Collapse via Item-vs-Page Diagnosis: Hacker Week 自己去找 search ranker 在哪 silently failing -- dashboard 显示健康但 multi-intent query 比如 "pokemon" 90%+ 返回 trading cards，而购买数据显示一半 buyer 要 games / toys / fig
- EX-14 | LLM Exploration --- Killing the Agentic Mandate with One Week of ROI Math: 2023 年 leadership 要 'upgrade to GenAI'，给 sandbox + API credits 自己探，没有 requirements、没有 LLM precedent；先用 1 周 feasibility 把 agentic search 路径用 ROI math 杀掉 -- 不能接 i
- EX-19 | Explaining A/B Test Confounder to PM --- Technical Communication: PM 想用 buyer-based A/B 平台做 seller conversion 测试，但同一搜索页 treated/untreated seller 商品混排导致 confounder；用具体类比说服 PM 理解问题，提出 time-of-day split 折中方案 | KEY FACTS: same-pag
- BLOG-03 | Cross-Org Boundary Defense via LLM Relevance Pipeline: Ads 团队要求共享 relevance 数据违反 org boundary；深挖发现真需求是验证 A/B 结果，构建 LLM relevance pipeline 日产 ~18K 标签 ~$500 替代人工标注 | KEY FACTS: ~18K 标签/天 ~$500 | 人工标注 $0.30-0.80/条 | or

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 在给定技术栈不可变 (LLM tokenizer 改不了, 搜索解析器改不了) 的强约束下, 能否跳出直接修补的惯性, 从问题表征层面 (representation layer) 重构路径。L5 bar 是解法能抽象成可复用的模式, 并为组织留下 '下次遇见 mismatch 时可以考虑 proxy-layer' 的 mental model。
what_good_looks_like: 明确约束: LLM 端不能改 (生成成本/效果), 搜索端不能改 (核心 infra 迭代周期长) -- EX-09 primary 动作: 'zero changes to the search engine' 是强信号。
将问题从 '怎么让 LLM 输出搜索引擎理解的 query' reframe 成 '怎么让搜索系统消费 LLM 产出的语义表征' -- EX-09 primary 动作: 'discovered the proxy item approach: have the LLM generate descriptions of ideal items'。
利用现有资产最大化复用: embedding search, retrieval pipelines 全部不动, proxy item 只是新插入的中间产物 -- 这是 creative 的资源效率。
结果锚定到 unblocking 速度: 'fastest path to unblocking experimentation', 强调 time-to-experiment 是 success metric, 不是离线指标。
what_L5_adds: 解法抽象成一个可迁移的适配层模式: 以后遇到任何 '两种表征不兼容' 的场景 (如 knowledge graph -> query, 用户画像 -> ranking), 都可以考虑插入 proxy-rep layer, 这是 L5 对组织架构的影响, 不是一次性技巧。
对约束的主动审计: 我不但找到了方案, 而且还评估了 alternative 的成本 (retraining / fixing LLM query 要几个月), 并且在行动中明确传递 '最优路径是基于现有资源的创造性重用'。
跨团队 ripple effect: proxy item success 之后, 这个模式可能被其他集成 LLM 的团队复用, 我在组织内留下了 knowledge artifact, 不是一个人用完就藏起来。
common_failure_modes: 把 'creative' 讲成 '我试了很多 prompt 终于找到一个好使的' -- 这没有改变问题框架, 只是参数探索, reviewer 会判定为 trial-and-error, 不符合 L5 定义。
没有解释为什么直接途径不可行, 导致 creative solution 看起来像是为了炫技而绕远路, 缺少 'given constraints' 的理解。
结果模糊: '它效果好多了' 但没说 unblock 了哪个实验/团队, 花了多久, reviewer 无法 verify impact -- EX-09 的 strong signal 是 'fastest path to unblocking experimentation'。
把成功归因于运气或突发灵感, 而非结构化的诊断过程 (root cause -> 可选路径树 -> 选择最利用现有资产的方案), 缺乏 L5 的 process transparency。

text: Give an example of a time when you analyzed a complex problem and broke it down.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Problem Solving & Data-Driven Decisions): Give an example of a time when you analyzed a complex problem and broke it down.

[PRIMARY] EX-03 | Challenging Sale NDCG Proxy — First Principles Rethinking
  situation: Our search ranking team was optimizing Sale NDCG -- an industry-standard metric -- but I discovered it systematically prioritized cheap items over expensive ones, causing a \$100 necklace to rank below \$5 accessories despite generating far more marketplace value.
  task: I needed to identify the correct optimization proxy and convince the team and stakeholders that the existing industry-standard approach was fundamentally flawed.
  action: - Analyzed the relationship between item price and ranking position; demonstrated that Sale NDCG's conversion-rate weighting created systematic price bias - Proposed GMB (price x sale probability) as the correct optimization target -- this directly measures marketplace value, not just conversion likelihood - Discovered a deeper calibration trap: the model's group-level probabilities looked correct, but individual item scores were insensitive to item-level differences, causing price alone to dominate - Designed a BM25-inspired price transformation with log scaling and per-tranche soft caps -- c
  result: Switching to GMB proxy fundamentally improved ranking behavior. High-quality, authenticated listings saw significant GMB uplift, and the insight that **"proxy selection is the most underestimated ML decision"** became a guiding principle for the entire team's future work.
  evidence_quotes: ["Proxy 选择是 ML 项目里最被低估的决策", "100 刀首饰的 conversion rate 可以高于 5 刀商品的 5 倍", "问题不在于模型选型，而在于 pointwise 框架本身的建模假设是错的"]
  cn_elevator_pitch: 发现 Sale NDCG 系统性偏向低价商品——$5 配饰排在 $100 项链前面；提出 GMB (price x sale probability) 作为正确 proxy，揭示 calibration 陷阱 | KEY FACTS: Sale NDCG 价格偏差 | GMB proxy 替代 | calibration 陷阱 | "proxy 选择是最被低估的 ML 决策"

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- EX-23 | Large-Scale Project with Tight Deadlines --- NYC C2C Policy Launch: NYC C2C 业务持续下滑，VP 要求 2 周内出测试、1 月内出 launch 方案，30+ 人跨组协调；测试上线后发现 control 失效——upstream 团队"修复" incident 时覆盖了 control property；进一步发现 combo-launch 各 policy 互相抵消，推动逐项上
- EX-05 | Relevance Filtering: Deployment Feasibility Under Latency Constraints: 作为唯一 MLE 发现 XGBoost 模型 +10% latency 远超 <=1% 预算；三路方案中两路失败，最终 cheap rejection + early exit 组合达标 | KEY FACTS: +10% latency vs <=1% 预算 | cheap rejection + early exi

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 能否把一个 hairy problem 拆成可独立诊断的 layers, 并找到 root cause frame (不是 symptom cluster)。L5 bar 是能从 proxy/assumption 层面拆解系统性 bias, 而不是停在 data pattern 描述。
what_good_looks_like: Breakdown 有清晰的 layers: EX-03 primary 动作: 'Analyzed the relationship between item price and ranking position; demonstrated that Sale NDCG's conversion-rate weighting created systematic price bias' -- 这是 layer 1 (symptom)。
Layer 2 是 root mechanism: 'Proposed GMB (price x sale probability) as the correct optimization target' -- 直接攻击 proxy 定义, 不是参数。

Layer 3 是 deeper calibration trap: 'The model's group-level probabilities looked correct, but individual item scores were insensitive to item-level differences, causing price alone to dominate' -- 这是 self-audit 自己的 learning system, 不是外部 blame。
Lesson 落到 team-level principle: 'proxy selection is the most underestimated ML decision' -- 把单一问题的拆解结果变成可转移的 org asset, 这是 L5 需要的 generativity。
what_L5_adds: 从 problem decomposition 到 decision architecture: 不仅是 '这个 metric 有问题', 而是 'proxy selection is an ML design decision that is systematically under-emphasized in our team' -- L5 的 frame 抬到 org learning 层。
能识别自己的 model 里 hidden hierarchy of assumptions (e.g. group calibration vs item-level sensitivity), 然后 isolate 出哪个 assumption 导致了 failure -- 这不是 data analysis skill, 是 model humility。
对 industry-standard (Sale NDCG) 的挑战不是 contrarian, 而是 grounded in business value -- GMB 直接 map to marketplace value, 不是 academic proxy 争论, L5 reviewer 需要看到 business anchoring。
common_failure_modes: 停留在 data exploration: 'I ran SQL, looked at histograms, found something, fixed it' -- 没有 proxy-level / assumption-level 拆解, reviewer 看不到 L5 的 structural 思维。
把 breakdown 讲成 linear recipe: '第一步看数据, 第二步找原因, 第三步 fix' -- 实际 complex problem 的 decomposition 是 iterative + reframing, linear 叙述会 kill depth。
Lesson 太本地化: '从这个 case 我学到了 price matters' -- 没有 generalize 成 principle (e.g. 'proxy selection is the most underestimated'), reviewer 无法 imagine reuse。
只 address symptom 不 address confound: 如果 candidate 只说 '我们加了 price feature 就解决了', 没提 calibration trap, 那 decomposition 就停在 first-order, 属于 L4 答案。

text: Describe a situation where you had to make a tough trade-off to keep a project moving forward.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Problem Solving & Data-Driven Decisions): Describe a situation where you had to make a tough trade-off to keep a project moving forward.

[PRIMARY] EX-05 | Relevance Filtering: Deployment Feasibility Under Latency Constraints
  situation: As tech lead and sole MLE on a relevance filtering project, my team spent two months building a high-accuracy XGBoost model with thousands of trees. At deployment time, we discovered the model added +10% latency overhead -- completely unacceptable against our <=1% budget.
  task: Find a model architecture that met the strict <=1% latency constraint while maintaining acceptable filtering accuracy -- and ensure it actually worked end-to-end in production.
  action: Beat 1 -- Tried three paths, two died. I laid out three approaches: early exit (truncate tree evaluation at convergence depth ~600 trees), feature-pruned small model (retrain with only top-importance features), and cheap rejection (lightweight model rejects obvious cases, passes hard cases to full model). Feature-pruned model lost too much accuracy -- eliminated. Early exit alone landed right at the latency boundary with no safety margin.  Beat 2 -- Key insight: most requests don't need the big model. I went back to the production traffic distribution and noticed something others hadn't focuse
  result: Shipped the feature meeting the <=1% latency target. GMB on null/low-intent queries improved +4-6%. The cheap rejection + early exit pattern was later reused for two other model deployments. The silent failure lesson led me to establish a new practice: before any launch, run an end-to-end payload stress test verifying that model outputs are received intact at every downstream stage -- not just 'ca
  evidence_quotes: ["Over-invested in deep models (thousands of trees) before confronting latency budgets — as sole MLE I should have set the deployment envelope first", "Engineering deployability is the real constraint — fancy ideas fail when the underlying system relies on heavy caching or offline precomputation"]
  cn_elevator_pitch: 作为唯一 MLE 发现 XGBoost 模型 +10% latency 远超 <=1% 预算；三路方案中两路失败，最终 cheap rejection + early exit 组合达标 | KEY FACTS: +10% latency vs <=1% 预算 | cheap rejection + early exit | +4-6% GMB on null/low-intent | end-to-end payload 验证新实践

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: trade-off 是否基于 data-driven 的 concrete metric trade, 而不是主观的 'it felt right'。L5 bar 是从单次 trade-off 中提炼出可复现的 decision framework, 并将隐性风险 (silent failure) 升级为系统性 guardrail。
what_good_looks_like: Trade-off 有两条 explicit constraint 线: EX-05 primary 动作: 'latency 不超过 1% budget' vs 'filtering accuracy', 每一步 path 的 kill/promote 都基于这两个 metric 的实测数据, 不是 opinion。
探索阶段 show real failures: 三条路径中两条因 accuracy 或 margin 不够被明确剔除, 每条失败都有量化止损线, 这些失败公开说出来本身是 credibility。
Solution 是 compound, 不是 pick-one: cheap rejection 解决 '大模型只用于少数情况', early exit 解决 '截断深度', 两件合在一起才满足约束, 体现 design composability。
Post-shipment 有 data-backed impact: +4-6% GMB on null/low-intent queries, 把 trade-off 的 gain 锚定在 business outcome 上, 不是技术指标自娱。
what_L5_adds: 从一次权衡中 extract 出组织级实践: 提出了 'end-to-end payload stress test 验证模型输出在所有下游 stage 的 integrity', 把 silent failure 风险从 个人经验升级为流程性 guardrail。
Trade-off 的 framing 超越单项目: cheap rejection + early exit 的 pattern 后来被两个其他模型部署复用, 证明这是 class-level 的解决方案, 不是一次 patch。
Self-correction 在上游: '作为 sole MLE 我应该在设计模型前先定部署 envelope' 是对 process 的 reframe, 体现 L5 级别的 design constraint ordering 意识。
common_failure_modes: Trade-off 没有 hard metric: '我凭经验觉得这样能 work', 没有 latency 数字/accuracy drop 数字, reviewer 会判定为拍脑袋, 直接 downgrade。
把不得不做的妥协讲成主动选择: 比如说 '我故意选了简单模型因为它更好 maintain' -- 实际是被 latency 逼的, 掩盖 real constraint 会让 reviewer 质疑 honesty。
没有展示探索 dead-end: 只说 '我找到了 cheap rejection 完美解决', 不说其他路径的失败, 变成 smooth sailing 故事, 失去 trade-off toughness 本质。
Impact 只有技术指标: 'latency 达标' 就结束, 没有 business outcome 如 GMB/CTR lift, review 会觉得我停留在 engineer 视角, 不是 L5 的产品-sense 水平。

text: Tell me about a time when you managed a large-scale project with tight deadlines.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Execution & Project Management): Tell me about a time when you managed a large-scale project with tight deadlines.

[PRIMARY] EX-23 | Large-Scale Project with Tight Deadlines --- NYC C2C Policy Launch
  situation: Our NYC C2C business had been declining for weeks as competitors captured market share, and the VP demanded a test within 2 weeks and a launch proposal within 1 month -- with 30+ people across the org needing to coordinate.
  task: As project lead, needed to deliver a policy test and launch framework under extremely tight timeline, while maintaining daily updates and weekly VP meeting cadence.
  action: - Inventoried all workstreams, identified the critical path, and organized work so 30+ people didn't block each other - After test launch, discovered control effectiveness was below expectations. Team suspected Kafka logging fluctuation, but while fixing logging I continued digging deeper - Discovered root cause: upstream web gateway team had silently "fixed" an incident by overwriting our control property -- causing silent test failure that would have invalidated all results - Found a deeper structural issue: multiple policies that tested successfully independently **competed for the same top
  result: Project **delivered within the VP's deadline**. More critically, I prevented the team from making a costly mistake: blindly combo-launching all policies would have shown disappointing results (policies canceling each other), potentially killing good individual policies based on a flawed combined test. The scope adjustment ensured the **highest-impact policies launched cleanly**, and the allocation
  evidence_quotes: ["VP demanded test within 2 weeks, launch proposal within 1 month, 30+ person project", "Upstream gateway team silently fixed an incident by overwriting control property", "Multiple policies competed for top slots when combo-launched"]
  cn_elevator_pitch: NYC C2C 业务持续下滑，VP 要求 2 周内出测试、1 月内出 launch 方案，30+ 人跨组协调；测试上线后发现 control 失效——upstream 团队"修复" incident 时覆盖了 control property；进一步发现 combo-launch 各 policy 互相抵消，推动逐项上线避免好 policy 被误杀 | KEY FACTS: 2 周 deadline + 30 人协调 | silent control 覆盖 | combo-launch 互相抵消 | 逐项上线策略

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- EX-01 | Search Diversity --- Intent Collapse via Item-vs-Page Diagnosis: Hacker Week 自己去找 search ranker 在哪 silently failing -- dashboard 显示健康但 multi-intent query 比如 "pokemon" 90%+ 返回 trading cards，而购买数据显示一半 buyer 要 games / toys / fig
- EX-05 | Relevance Filtering: Deployment Feasibility Under Latency Constraints: 作为唯一 MLE 发现 XGBoost 模型 +10% latency 远超 <=1% 预算；三路方案中两路失败，最终 cheap rejection + early exit 组合达标 | KEY FACTS: +10% latency vs <=1% 预算 | cheap rejection + early exi

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 在大规模跨组/hard deadline 压力下, execution 是否只停在做完, 还是能在 delivery 过程中 detect silent failures 并做 scope pivot 保全 high-impact outcomes。L5 bar 是能在 VP-imposed 高压下 resist '只管 delivery' 的 reflex, 主动 identify systemic risk 并 change course, 体现对 business KPI 而非单一 on-time metric 的 ownership。
what_good_looks_like: 提前 inventory 所有 workstreams 并 identify critical path, 明确展示 30+ 人如何不会互相 block (EX-23 的 organizing work so 30+ people didn't block each other)。
发现表面 symptom (control 失效 / Kafka logging fluctuation) 后不停留于表层修复, 而是持续 dig deeper 找到 root cause: upstream gateway 覆盖 control property。这是 L5 的 detective instinct。
EX-23 primary 动作: 发现 combo-launch 时多个 independently successful policies 会 compete for same top slots 彼此抵消, 主动做 scope adjustment 改为逐项上线, 避免好 policy 被 flawed combined test 误杀。
在 VP 的 2-week test / 1-month launch 硬 deadline 下, 建立 daily updates + weekly VP meeting cadence, 体现 project management 的 rhythm, 不使用 hero-mode patches 冲线。
what_L5_adds: 从 tracking delivery 到 systemic risk detection: 识别出多个 policies combo-launch 在共享 ranking surface 上会互斥, 这是 org-level 的 tradeoff 认知, 不是单个 workstream 的 task 完成度。
在 VP-imposed timeline 压力下, 敢于 propose scope adjustment 而非 gamble 在 flawed combined test 上, 体现的是对 business KPI (highest-impact policies launch cleanly) 的 ownership, 而非对 schedule reputation 的防卫。
30+ 人 cross-functional 场景: 不是一对一 unblock, 而是建立 cadence (daily/weekly) 让信息在 org-wide 流动, 避免出现第二个 'upstream silently overwrote our property' 这类 left-hand-not-talking-to-right-hand failure。
common_failure_modes: 一个完美按时交付的 story, 没有任何意外或风险: reviewer 直接判断 project 没有 real stakes 或 candidate 没能力 detect what was going wrong, 扣分。
只停留在 issue solved 层面 (如 'Kafka 波动修复完毕'), 没有深挖到 deeper structural problem (如 competing policies / upstream overwrite), 形同 junior ops 报告, 不到 L5 bar。
面对 tight deadline 选择牺牲 quality 强行 delivery, 不讲 tradeoff 和 business impact 判断, reviewer 会认为 candidate 只对 schedule 负责, 不对 outcome 负责。
30+ 人规模只作为背景数字出现, 不提任何协调机制或信息同步方式, 看起来像 solo execution 而非 project lead, 缺乏 cross-team leverage 证据。

text: Explain a complex technical problem you solved and your approach.
primary_rendered:

[PRIMARY] EX-05 | Relevance Filtering: Deployment Feasibility Under Latency Constraints

  task: Find a model architecture that met the strict <=1% latency constraint while maintaining acceptable filtering accuracy -- and ensure it actually worked end-to-end in production.
  action: Beat 1 -- Tried three paths, two died. I laid out three approaches: early exit (truncate tree evaluation at convergence depth ~600 trees), feature-pruned small model (retrain with only top-importance features), and cheap rejection (lightweight model rejects obvious cases, passes hard cases to full model). Feature-pruned model lost too much accuracy -- eliminated. Early exit alone landed right at the latency boundary with no safety margin.  Beat 2 -- Key insight: most requests don't need the big model. I went back to the production traffic distribution and noticed something others hadn't focuse
  result: Shipped the feature meeting the <=1% latency target. GMB on null/low-intent queries improved +4-6%. The cheap rejection + early exit pattern was later reused for two other model deployments. The silent failure lesson led me to establish a new practice: before any launch, run an end-to-end payload stress test verifying that model outputs are received intact at every downstream stage -- not just 'ca
  evidence_quotes: ["Over-invested in deep models (thousands of trees) before confronting latency budgets — as sole MLE I should have set the deployment envelope first", "Engineering deployability is the real constraint — fancy ideas fail when the underlying system relies on heavy caching or offline precomputation"]
  cn_elevator_pitch: 作为唯一 MLE 发现 XGBoost 模型 +10% latency 远超 <=1% 预算；三路方案中两路失败，最终 cheap rejection + early exit 组合达标 | KEY FACTS: +10% latency vs <=1% 预算 | cheap rejection + early exit | +4-6% GMB on null/low-intent | end-to-end payload 验证新实践

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 能不能讲清楚一个 complex technical problem 的 architecture / approach / tradeoff / result, 而不是停留在 '我写了个模型'。L5 bar 是能在 solution 层面体现 design-time 的 constraints-first 思维 (latency budget / system envelope), 并在 success 后提取 reusable pattern 或 organizational practice。
what_good_looks_like: Problem complexity 明确: 不是 '模型精度低', 而是 latency +10% vs budget 不超过 1% + 模型已训练 + 作为唯一 MLE 必须找到一条 deployable path。EX-05 primary 动作: 'as sole MLE I should have set the deployment envelope first' -- 承认 framing error。
Approach 呈现实证: 三路并行探索 (early exit / feature-pruned / cheap rejection), 两路被 eliminate (accuracy loss / margin), 一路存活并组合 cheap rejection。必须 concretely 说出 each path 的死因, 不是 hand-waving。
Tradeoff 的可解释性: cheap rejection + early exit 怎么做到 latency 不超过 1% 同时保住 +4-6% GMB -- 这一点必须落到生产 traffic distribution 的 insight (most requests are null/low-intent)。
Result 有两层: (1) 业务指标 (GMB) + (2) organizataional learning -- 事后建立的 end-to-end payload stress test practice, 并提到该 pattern 被复用。
what_L5_adds: Design-time constraints-first 的反思: 不只是修 latency, 而是把 deployment envelope 作为 pre-design gate 引入后续任何 model work -- 这是从 single-point fix 到 organizational risk 的 shift。
Solution 抽象成 reusable pattern: cheap-rejection + early-exit cascaded 被迁移到其他两个 model deployment -- 这是 L5 应有的 leverage play, 不再是 one-off 英雄主义。
Systemic blind-spot 识别与 organizational fix: 发现 downstream 有 silent failure 后, 不是只加监控, 而是推动了 full payload stress test 的团队实践 -- 这是 ownership beyond IC role。
common_failure_modes: Problem 定义太浅: '模型性能不好, 我用了个更深的网络修好了' -- 缺少 latency / budget / tradeoff 的 frame, reviewer 会认为候选人缺乏 production 意识。
Approach 像游记: 罗列做过的事但不说失败路径和死因, 没有 try-kill 的迭代张力。Reviewer 直接推断这是 hindsight 重构。
Result 只有 accuracy 无业务指标: 只说 '模型精度提升 2%' 不说 GMB 或用户体验, Reviewer 无法 scale 这个 success 的重要性。
没有 organizational learning: 只停在 technical result, 不提该 pattern 对其他 team 的 leverage 或 build-time 流程改变 -- 这会被视为 L4-level 的 execution 描述。

QUESTION (Execution & Project Management): Describe a time when you dealt with a major project setback and how you recovered.

[PRIMARY] EX-33B | MoE Over-Iteration: A Model Believer's Humility Lesson on Problem Formulation
  situation: At eBay search I was a strong believer in the model-side narrative: the industry had moved toward whole-page optimization, neural ranking, and MoE architectures, and I shared the assumption that increasingly sophisticated rankers would unlock the diversity, abandonment, and exploration problems we were stuck on. Leadership assigned me ownership of a high-visibility project to migrate search from b
  task: Deliver a working MoE ranker that integrated multiple expert heads (conversion, abandonment, exploration) and demonstrated improvement on our org's launch criteria. My personal stake was even higher than the project scope: I had been advocating internally that model-side sophistication was the right
  action: (1) First wall - bias in expert routing. Initial training showed the gating network was collapsing onto the conversion expert and ignoring the others. I treated this as a technical bug: re-balanced training data, added auxiliary losses to encourage expert diversification, retrained. Bias reduced.  (2) Second wall - degraded MoE router behavior. After the bias fix, the router started oscillating - co-activating experts that were pulling in opposite directions. I again treated it as a tuning problem: more training rounds, careful warmup schedules, auxiliary load-balancing terms. The oscillation 
  result: The MoE direction did not launch. Technically the system was complete; business-wise the direction was wrong from day one because we had been asking the wrong question. I had burned ~80 GPU nodes of org-wide headroom, several quarters of my own time, and the implicit credibility I had built advocating for the model-side narrative. There was no rescue and no silver lining I could honestly offer. Th
  evidence_quotes: ["The system was tech-unblocked but business-unlaunchable.", "I was fixing one wall after another -- bias, router, orthogonal expert -- and that pattern itself should have told me the problem was not where I was looking.", "No amount of further model iteration would fix it, because the problem was n
  cn_elevator_pitch: 作为 model believer 在 MoE 上层层迭代——修 bias、修 router、加正交 expert；耗尽 ~80 GPU 后认清 BI/GMB 是真 KPI，MRR 是 self-fulfilling proxy | KEY FACTS: ~80 GPU 节点 | BI + GMB 真 KPI | MRR 不是 KPI | 技术 unblocked 但 business unlaunchable

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- EX-23 | Large-Scale Project with Tight Deadlines --- NYC C2C Policy Launch: NYC C2C 业务持续下滑，VP 要求 2 周内出测试、1 月内出 launch 方案，30+ 人跨组协调；测试上线后发现 control 失效——upstream 团队"修复" incident 时覆盖了 control property；进一步发现 combo-launch 各 policy 互相抵消，推动逐项上

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 能否直面一次真正的重大挫折----不是那种藏着 rescue tail 的 setback, 而是方向性错误----并从中提炼出可迁移的 problem formulation 级的教训。L5 bar 是能展示从 execution failure 到 frame-level pivot 的认知跃迁, 而不是补救或 blame-shift。
what_good_looks_like: Clean failure 的坦白: 'There was no rescue and no silver lining I could honestly offer.' 这种直接承认没有回收/没有粉饰的表述, 是 L5 区别于 junior 编造 redemption 的核心。EX-33B primary 动作: 交付了技术完整但 business-unlaunchable 的 MoE, 不 attempt 事后解释成 '其实学到了很多'。
具体量化 blast radius: ~80 GPU 节点 / 几个季度的时间 / 个人 advocacy 积累的 implicit credibility, 不是 '花了一些资源'。这种 scale 让 reviewer 相信 story 的真实性。
Setback 的 root cause 定位在问题定义层: 不是 '调参没调好', 而是 '我们一直在问错误的问题----MRR 是 self-fulfilling proxy'。这展示了对业务假设的重新审视。
Recovery 不是 project recovery 而是 cognitive recovery: 从 model believer 到 'problem formulation first' 的 humility lesson, 并能将其结构化, 未来可 transfer 到其他项目----先验证 KPI 定义, 再投身工程。
what_L5_adds: Frame-level pivot: L4 可能会说 '我下次多调参 / 多讨论', L5 则跳出来问 '我们是不是在用错误的目标函数?' 并敢于在组织内提出这个质疑, 即使自己曾是 evangelist。
Org-level self-audit: 不只算 personal cost (~80 GPU 个人心疼), 而是作为组织资源用户, 意识到这种方向错误是 shared infra / shared strategy 的风险, 并可能推动早期 KPI alignment 的决策机制。
Self-awareness beyond humility: 不满足于 '我错了, 以后不独断', 而是解剖 '为什么我会成为 model believer'----那种认知偏误的源头 (如高 velocity 合作 loop 带来的 invincibility), 并警示自己 repeat pattern。
common_failure_modes: 虚假 rescue tail: 强行说 '虽然没 launch 但我的代码后来被用了' 或 '我学到了新的调参方法'----reviewer 会看出这是在粉饰, 缺乏面对重大失败的 authenticity。
Scapegoating via context: 'PM/leadership 给的 KPI 不对 / 团队没质疑我 / 业界 trend 就这样'----把责任外化, 失去 ownership 得分。L5 要求 blame 留在自己的 assumptions 上。
没有具体 scale: 只说 '花了很长时间 / 很多资源' 而没有 ~80 GPU 节点这种具体数字, reviewer 会觉得 setback 太小或故事是编的。
Lesson 停在战术层: '下次我要设置更小的离线实验' / '要更早拉人 review'----这些是不够的; L5 的答案要求指向 problem framing 的 default shift (e.g. 区分北星指标和 proxy 指标的真实危害)。

text: How do you balance immediate tasks with longer-term projects?
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Execution & Project Management): How do you balance immediate tasks with longer-term projects?

[PRIMARY] EX-21 | Tech Debt Balance --- Declarative Artifactory Proof of Concept
  situation: Features I was building required the team's new declarative artifactory system, but that system was repeatedly delayed with no clear timeline -- blocking feature delivery that the business needed now.
  task: Find a path that unblocks feature delivery without creating a throwaway workaround. Core question: which values of the declarative system can be captured now, so the work remains aligned with long-term architecture?
  action: - Deep research revealed the declarative system's architectural essence: the core value is generating a JSON ranking rule expression; the blockers were peripheral infrastructure (storage, versioning, deployment) -- not the expression generation itself - Designed approach using an internal caching system for storage, injecting named expressions as parameters into the search engine - Built parity tests proving hand-generated expressions were **identical** to what the declarative system's profiling layer would generate -- hard evidence, not promises - Demoed equivalence to the team; declarative t
  result: Feature **shipped on time** with business win, rather than being blocked for a year. When the declarative system finally became ready, migration was smooth -- the core expression implementation was already consistent, requiring only storage/versioning migration. The interim solution effectively became **early validation for the declarative system itself**. Key thesis: tech debt isn't a "fast vs. c
  evidence_quotes: ["Tech debt is not a fast-vs-clean binary --- it is whether you truly understand the system's architectural essence", "Identified boundary between core (named expr generation) and peripheral (storage/versioning/deployment infrastructure)", "Parity test provided hard evidence that hand-generated name
  cn_elevator_pitch: 新功能依赖团队 declarative artifactory 系统但长期 delay 无 timeline；深入研究发现核心价值是 JSON ranking rule expression generation，blocker 是周边 infra；用内部 caching 系统做 storage，功能按时交付且后续迁移无缝衔接 | KEY FACTS: 核心 vs 周边分离 | parity tests 验证一致性 | 按时交付 vs 等一年 | 迁移仅需 storage/versioning 切换

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- EX-06 | Allocation Framework as Reusable Platform Primitive — 200M+ Impact: 从 diversity +1% GMB 单点实验识别出平台化机会；设计 reusable allocation primitive——caching + deficit calculation + uplift，替换 LTR scoring 为 ads-style bidding + allocation 范式 | K

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 遇到 short-term delivery 被 long-term dependency 阻塞时, 是等待/绕过/重构, 以及如何做 tradeoff 决策。L5 bar 是不把 tradeoff 当成个人优先级排列, 而是先解剖 long-term 的 architectural essence, 然后 抽取核心价值部分提前交付, 让短期收益成为长期系统的 early validation。
what_good_looks_like: 区分核心价值与周边阻塞: EX-21 primary 动作: 深入研究后发现 declarative 系统的核心是 JSON ranking rule expression generation, 周边 infrastructure (storage / versioning / deployment) 才是 delay 根源, 因此 decouple 二者, 先交付核心。
用 hard evidence 而不是 credo 说服 team: EX-21 primary 动作: 构建 parity tests 证明手写表达式与 declarative 系统会生成的完全一致, 消除了团队对 future misalignment 的恐惧。
Tradeoff 边界清晰可逆: 清晰定义 what 会被复用的 (core expression) vs what 会成为 future migration tax (storage layer), 迁移成本量化 (只需切换 storage / versioning layer), 不是一笔 all-or-nothing 的赌注。
Not just 'I shipped', but 'what the org learned': 最终迁移平滑, 短期方案变成了 declarative 系统的 early validation, 为组织留存了可迁移的模式。
what_L5_adds: 把 '我做完了短期任务' 升华为 '我解剖了 long-term 的内部结构并做外科手术式解耦' -- reviewer 看到的是架构判断力, 不是多任务处理能力。
主动管理 future sunk cost risk: 如果 declarative 系统最终流产, my temporary cache-based solution 会不会成为 toxic legacy? L5 会在设计时就让方案具备 '可废弃性' (采用内部 caching 系统做 storage 而非自建), 降低组织 risk。
Pattern 沉淀: parity test 成为团队后续评估 partial adoption 的模板, 这是从个人 tradeoff 到 org-level capability 的 lift。
common_failure_modes: 个人时间管理框架: 答案讲 'I use priorities / time blocks' 而不涉及技术 tradeoff 决策, reviewer 判定在讲 execution 而非 project management。
声称同时完成但没 tradeoff honesty: 'I worked nights and did both' 看似 dedication 但没展示判断力, L5 bar 要的是 informed tradeoff, 不是 endurance。
只说 'I pushed back on the dependency' 但无 influence 路径: 没有展示用 data / parity proof 说服团队接收 partial adoption 的 influence 动作, 只是 claim pushback 会被认为没有 cross-team 推动力。
方案不留退路: 临时方案完全 bypass long-term 系统, 迁移成本爆炸, 但候选人未觉知 future cost -- reviewer 会判定缺乏 long-term 视野。

text: Describe a time when you coached or mentored someone.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Leadership & People Development): Describe a time when you coached or mentored someone.

[PRIMARY] EX-12 | Helping PhD Interns Transition from Notebook to Production Stack
  situation: PhD interns were keeping GPU instances running 24/7 to avoid resource reclamation, causing burnout risk, because they were only comfortable with Jupyter notebooks and struggled to adapt to the production environment.
  task: I needed to help interns adapt to the internal production tech stack while addressing the unhealthy work pattern of keeping instances alive around the clock.
  action: - Directly addressed the unhealthy pattern: explained that resources should only be allocated during active job runs, not kept alive continuously - Identified the real barriers: no in-memory data review capability, need for more tests, high cost of single-run failures, dependency management complexity - Built a template class: loads raw logging data -> generates dataset -> runs a simple LR model, covering the full production workflow in one reusable example - Personally walked through the migration despite resistance from researchers who saw it as unnecessary overhead
  result: Interns **successfully adapted** to the production stack and stopped the unsustainable 24/7 pattern. The template became a **reusable onboarding resource for the entire research team**, enabling any new researcher to go from notebook prototype to production-ready code independently.
  evidence_quotes: []
  cn_elevator_pitch: PhD interns 因不熟 production stack 保持 GPU 实例 24/7 运行避免回收；识别真正障碍（无 in-memory 数据审查、dependency 复杂），构建 template class 覆盖 raw data -> dataset -> model 全流程，成为研究团队 reusable onboarding 资源 | KEY FACTS: 24/7 GPU 占用 -> 正常工作模式 | template class 全流程覆盖 | notebook -> production 迁移 | 团队级 onboarding 复用

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- EX-11 | Mentoring Intern on Overpromise / Goal Visibility: PhD intern 实际进度不错但 peer 感知"只有 self-learning 没有 deadline"；通过 1:1 正面引导建立 goals-progress-confidence 汇报框架，弥合 academia-to-industry 沟通鸿沟，intern 最终拿到 return offer | KE

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 能否从 'I taught someone a skill' 升维到 'I enabled someone's growth by diagnosing their real blockers and left a scalable asset for the team'。L5 bar 是 coaching 的 impact 不止于个体, 更放大到 org-level 可复用性 (template/process/framework), 并展现对 mentee 内部动机 (而不是表面行为) 的精准介入。
what_good_looks_like: First-person 介入 root cause, 不满足于表层症状: EX-12 primary 动作 'Identified the real barriers: no in-memory data review capability, need for more tests, high cost of single-run failures, dependency management complexity', 而不是只说 'they were used to notebooks'。
Concrete output 可复用: 留下 template class 作为 onboarding artifact, 证明 impact 从 1-on-1 放大到 team-level self-service。
Empathy with boundary: 直接点出 24/7 不健康模式, 但不 judge 动机, 而是把问题 frame 成 engineering gap, 既保护关系又推动改变。
Result 已 内化 + 独立: interns 成功适应生产栈 并 停止 24/7, 说明 coaching 已转化为 autonomous capability, 不是依赖我的持续干预。
what_L5_adds: 从个体指导跳转到团队资产: L4 会手把手教, L5 会问 '为什么这群 smart people 会 stuck? 缺什么 reusable component 能 unblock 后续所有人?' 然后 build that component。
Diagnose mental-model gap, not skill gap: 实习生不是不会写 production code, 而是 research 环境缺失快速迭代的安全感 (in-memory 观察 / 低失败成本) -- L5 识别并补齐环境的心理模型, 而不是贴 '学一下 spark' 标签。
Owning the coaching arc end-to-end: 看到 unhealthy pattern (24/7 GPU) -> 不听之任之 -> 顶着 researcher 的阻力直接 walk through migration -> 直到对方能独立, 这是一种 firm care, 区别于 L4 的 '我建议了但对方不听就算了' 的 passivity。
common_failure_modes: Coaching 变成 teaching 清单: '我教他们用了 Git, Docker, Kubernetes' -- 只展示技术传递, 没展示 mentee 动机或障碍, reviewer 会判定缺乏 people awareness。
Mentee 没有真正的成长证据: 故事停在 '我给他们做了培训', 没有 'they then independently did X', 导致 impact 不可验证。
过于软性, 没有 tension: 'mentee 很配合, 学得很快, 皆大欢喜' -- 缺乏 real barrier 的 coaching 对 L5 来说太浅, 体现不出应对阻力 / 怀疑的能力。
把 mentee 工具化: 讲自己为了完成项目才教人, 结果聚焦在自己项目成功而不是 mentee 成长 -- reviewer 看不到 people-first 的 leadership。

text: Tell me about a time you had to make a tough call as a leader.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Leadership & People Development): Tell me about a time you had to make a tough call as a leader.

[PRIMARY] BLOG-04 | Goal Tracking Reform: Honest Metrics Over Cosmetic Delivery
  situation: Our team's goal tracking system was quietly rewarding failure. Teams would rename unfinished goals, re-scope deliverables mid-cycle, and roll them over -- so on paper, delivery rates looked healthy, but actual velocity was declining quarter over quarter.
  task: As a stakeholder who reviewed these updates weekly, I took it on myself to fix how we set, tracked, and evaluated goals -- so that our metrics reflected reality instead of masking it.
  action: - Diagnosed the root cause: updates were filled with jargon that blocked peer review, progress never mapped back to prior commitments, and "delivery" often just meant giving an old goal a new name - Proposed locking goal scope after kickoff and requiring peer confidence estimates against the original timeline -- not the reshuffled version - Manager pushed back, worried this would strain relationships with partner teams. She challenged me to design a proposal the whole group could accept - Key insight: reframed goal-setting itself -- for high-uncertainty projects, teams would commit to "develop
  result: Short-term delivery rates dropped -- which was exactly the proof the system was working, because previously hidden problems were now surfacing. At the VP prioritization level, macro velocity improved: we eliminated the cycle of disguised rollover goals and teams started setting commitments they could actually keep. The framework was later adopted by other orgs under Search.
  cn_elevator_pitch: 团队 goal tracking 暗中奖励失败——改名、re-scope、rollover 伪装交付率；推动锁定 scope + peer confidence estimates，短期交付率下降反证系统生效 | KEY FACTS: 锁定 goal scope | peer confidence estimates | 短期交付率下降 = 系统生效 | VP 级 velocity 改善

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- EX-13 | Authorship Dispute --- Navigating Conflict and Establishing Norms: 同事仅写不到一页 incomplete manuscript 却要求 first authorship；坚持"authorship 反映实际贡献，不做 gift"原则，准备学术伦理文献后 escalate 到双方 manager，建立 contribution-based 署名规范，后续再无争议 | KEY FACTS
- EX-34 | BBE Risk Policy: Seller-Level vs Listing-Level — Disagreeing with a Principal Researcher on Absolutism as Lazy Non-Action: 在 BBE 项目和 principal researcher disagree on seller-level 绝对风险 policy；用新卖家/小卖家 false-positive 数据 + '绝对标准是 lazy non-action 伪装'重新框定问题；落地 listing-level + cumulative

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: tough call 的 trade-off 有多 real, 你是否愿意承担短期可见的负面后果 (比如 metrics 下降 / 关系紧张) 来换取长期系统健康, 并且能否通过 influence 而非 authority 让 stakeholders 接受。L5 bar 是能识别组织层面的隐性 incentive (goal tracking 奖励失败), 并 reframe 游戏规则, 而不是在既定框架内做 optimization。
what_good_looks_like: Tough call 的 short-term pain 必须 explicit: BLOG-04 primary 动作: 'Short-term delivery rates dropped -- which was exactly the proof the system was working, because previously hidden problems were now surfacing.' 把 negative 指标重构为 positive signal。
Stakeholder pushback 不是通过 escalation 压制, 而是通过 reframe scope 化解: 经理 pushback 后, 不是妥协, 而是把方案 reframe 为 'high-uncertainty 项目 commit to develop impact prototype' -- 在对方 frame 里找到解法。
Call 的起源有清晰的 diagnostic lens: 不是 'I decided to set better goals', 而是 'I diagnosed goal tracking was quietly rewarding failure', 展示 pattern-recognition 而不是 reaction。
结果有组织层面的 follow-through: 不只是本团队采纳, 还写到 'framework was later adopted by other orgs under Search', 证明这个 tough call 有 structural impact。
what_L5_adds: 把 tough call 从 '说服某人' 提升到 'reframe 系统机制': L5 不是选 A 或 B, 而是重新定义游戏规则 (goal-setting 本身), 改变团队如何定义和跟踪成功。
在上级 pushback 时展现的 upstream influence: 经理挑战后, 不是退缩也不是 escalate, 而是 'challenged me to design a proposal the whole group could accept' -- 能接受这个约束并设计出通用方案, 这是 L5 的管理成熟度。
面对短期 metric 下降有 cheerleader 的勇气: L5 要能解释 'delivery rate 下降是健康的', 并为 VP 级别的 velocity 改善做 narrative, 不只是团队内部的交付指标。
common_failure_modes: 选一个没有 real pushback 的决定: 'tough call' 只是自己在脑子里挣扎了一下, 没有任何 stakeholder 反对, 显得是 trivial choice, reviewer 无法看到 leadership。
选择收益远大于代价的 '假 tough call': 比如 '我决定重构代码, 短期慢但长期快', 这几乎没有组织冲突, 不是 leader 的 tough call, 是 engineer 的技术决策。
没有 visible 短期负面, 把 story 讲成 '我做了 brave decision 然后 everyone cheered': 缺少 BLOG-04 那种 'delivery rates dropped' 的代价展示, leadership 的 grit 没体现。
把 tough call 归结于个人 heroism 而不是 system 设计: '我就站出来说我们不能再这样了' -- 没有 diagnostic, 没有 process change, 只是个人勇气, 这停留在 L4 的 individual ownership。
